answer: At every close the beacon mints one sealed filing permit for each row four unrelated heads had already judged, then deals the permits out without replacement, one per key, each sealed to the key that draws it: no sibling may inherit it or answer in its place, and it is spent the moment its claim is judged. Permits grow with the crowd's own judged work and never with the crowd's size, so a farm's tenth head draws the last permit and its eleventh draws none, while an honest head draws one worth a full claim. Violet marks each sealed permit, and the river of permits fills one ripple at a time.
